t: Closeout Verification Pattern - Prove context capture

ex.pattern: When closing session, agent must ACTIVELY VERIFY and PROVE that all critical decisions/designs are captured for 100% recovery
ex.problem: Users feel anxiety that context will be lost between sessions. High-level lugs aren't enough - details matter. Half-baked ideas and untrackable features float out of scope.
solution: 1. Agent audits: what was discussed vs what was saved
3. Creates detailed design/spec lugs with ALL specifics
4. Shows user EXACTLY what was saved
5. User reviews and can append missing ideas
ex.behavior: On closeout: (1) Create high-level epic lug, (2) Create detailed design/spec lug with schemas/templates/decisions/UX/specifics, (3) SHOW user both lugs, (4) Invite review: "Did I miss anything?"
ex.example: Architecture refactor: Epic lug (10 components) + Design spec lug (folder structure, minification legend, file headers, schemas, UX scripts, migration details)
ex.impact: Removes user anxiety, builds trust, ensures nothing lost, allows collaborative refinement. Prevents scope drift from lost context.
ex.applies_to: ALL epics, stories, features - EVERY lug must be actionable and trackable
ex.critical_principle: Lugs are like issues for bugs, stories, tests, reviews. This level of actionability must be standard for ALL work, not just special cases.
verification_script: For each topic: where is it saved?
Are high-level decisions + low-level details both captured?
ex.actionability_requirement: Every epic/story lug needs enough detail that next session can execute without guessing. Schemas, templates, UX scripts, exact folder structures, field mappings - EVERYTHING.

t: Enforcement Hooks Pattern - Active vs Passive AI Instructions

ex.pattern: Convert passive AI instructions (AGENTS.md) into active enforcement through tool-specific hooks that inject requirements BEFORE AI sees user message
ex.problem: AGENTS.md says 'Brief User Automatically (without prompting)' but AI receives it as passive <system-reminder> context. Instructions are descriptive, not imperative. AI has discretion whether to follow.
ex.solution: Framework-level hooks that run BEFORE user message reaches AI. Hook injects MANDATORY directive with blocking language: 'CRITICAL: BEFORE responding, you MUST...'

implementation.trigger: First user message (detects via protocol_completed flag)
implementation.action: Generate Session Focus briefing from live WAI-State.json and WAI-Lugs.jsonl, inject MUST execute requirement, append user message

key_insights: Passive instructions (When you start, Automatically) don't force execution
System reminders are reference material, not commands
Hooks provide forcing function by modifying prompt BEFORE AI sees it
Detection logic (protocol_completed flag) enables one-time execution
Live data generation (parse lugs, apply prioritization) ensures fresh context
Blocking language (CRITICAL, MUST, BEFORE) creates imperative
ex.applies_to: ALL WAI projects across all AI tools (Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code Copilot, etc)

t: Policy: Session Goal Setting - Define Work Cycle Focus

ex.pattern: After Session Focus briefing, offer user to define specific goal(s) for this work cycle. Create focused epic lug from discussion. Clear completion = closeout + new thread.
ex.trigger: After showing Session Focus briefing and recommendations (on session start)
agent_behavior: 1. Show Session Focus briefing (Active Work, Verification Status, Context Health, Recommendations)
2. Offer: What specific goal(s) would you like to focus on for this work cycle?
3. Discuss with user to clarify scope, success criteria, constraints
4. Create epic lug (ty=epic) with:
- Clear title describing the goal
- priority=session_focus or priority=current_cycle
- Detailed ex field: scope, success_criteria, out_of_scope, approach, constraints
- verify_on_closeout=true
- session_id for tracking
5. Work within epic scope - say what we do, do what we say
6. When epic complete: recommend closeout + new thread
prevents: Unclear completion criteria (when are we done?)
Context bloat from too many topics in one thread
benefits: User feels in control of session direction
AI has clear mandate and boundaries
Both know when work cycle is complete
Natural thread restart points
Clean separation of concerns across sessions
Reduces anxiety (we know what we're doing and when we're done)

out_of_scope: Things we're NOT doing this cycle
ex.next_session: What to tackle after this epic completes

t: Policy: Session Epic Prioritization - Complete Before New Work

ex.pattern: When user defines session epic, prioritize completing it over new work. On closeout, check if epic completed - if not, keep flagged for next session.
agent_behavior: When user defines goal and epic lug is created:
- Set priority=session_focus or priority=before_next_epic
- Mark as current session work
- Prioritize this epic over backlog items
- Focus on completion, not starting new things
During session:
- Work within epic scope
- Resist scope creep to new topics
- If user wants new work, clarify: finish current epic first or defer it?
On closeout:
- Check epic success_criteria
- If ALL criteria met: mark s=closed, celebrate completion
- If INCOMPLETE: keep priority=before_next_epic, add incomplete flag
- Update epic with: progress made, remaining work, blockers
Next session start:
- Incomplete session epic shows in Flagged Priority section
- Recommend: Continue previous epic or start new one?
- User decides: resume or defer
prevents: Starting new work while session epic incomplete
Losing track of session goals across thread restarts
Incomplete epics getting buried in backlog
benefits: Clear focus: one epic at a time
Natural completion points
Session epic survives thread restarts
User sees continuity: we said we'd do X, did we finish?
AI maintains focus on current goal
closeout_checklist: 4. If incomplete: keep priority=before_next_epic, add notes
5. Show user: Epic status, what was accomplished, what remains

t: Policy: Lug ID Optimization - Short, Accessible, Collision-Resistant

benefits: Human-readable: can reference in conversation
Copy-paste friendly: fits in one visual chunk
Token efficient: saves 52 chars per ID
Still unique: 16 trillion combinations
URL-friendly: can use in links/commands
